title: An ADR that gives the run transcript a narrow palette of its own, as an exception to ADR 0039
name: transcript-adr
description:
ADR 0039 reserves colour for status. The session look needs more than that. Write `docs/adr/0064-*.md` naming two exceptions, with their limits: never the canvas, never the rest of the chrome.
1. The transcript palette (`--tx-tool --tx-result --tx-error --tx-think --tx-human`, plus a `--tx-pass` for the checklist ✓ instead of borrowing `--status-ready`). Tool and human are periwinkle/indigo (hue ~275), not turquoise.
2. Provider brand colours and logos in the run screen's model badge (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Mistral + neutral fallback), shown only there.
Record the default transcript font as JetBrains Mono + IBM Plex Sans, bundled through `@fontsource` (the user chose bundling over Google Fonts: local tool, offline, ADR 0008), with the system stack as fallback. Add the tokens to `apps/dashboard/src/theme.css` in OKLCH, dark and light, with the greyscale-separation argument ADR 0039 makes. Values come from the approved `docs/design/watch-the-run.html`. The existing no-hex test must still pass.

brief.approach:
The approved mockup `docs/design/watch-the-run.html` already holds every value. This node turns those values into a record and into tokens. It changes no component: session-shell, tool-blocks and session-statusbar consume the tokens later.

1. ADR. Write `docs/adr/0064-the-run-screen-gets-a-palette-and-a-typeface.md` in the shape of `docs/adr/0063-*.md` (Status: accepted, Date, and **Amends:** ADR 0039). It has Context, Decision and Consequences, and records two named exceptions to ADR 0039 §2, each with its limit: never the canvas, never the rest of the chrome, only the run screen (`apps/dashboard/src/logs/`).
   - Transcript palette: `--tx-tool`, `--tx-result`, `--tx-error`, `--tx-think`, `--tx-human`, `--tx-pass`.
     - Tool and human are periwinkle, hue 275.
     - Error is rose, 350.
     - Think is magenta, 325.
     - Result stays neutral.
     - The checklist ✓ gets its own `--tx-pass` token and stops borrowing `--status-ready`. A status colour inside the transcript would mean "ready", which it does not. Pick a hue that stays clear of 150 (ready), for example a desaturated teal-green around 165–170 with lower chroma, and check its greyscale distance.
     - Give the hue and lightness argument the way ADR 0039 §1 does: why each hue avoids 235 (running), 300 (blocked), 25 (danger) and 45 (held).
   - Provider brand colours: `--provider-anthropic`, `--provider-openai`, `--provider-google`, `--provider-mistral`, `--provider-other`, as OKLCH approximations of each brand. They appear only in the model badge in the run screen's title bar, next to that provider's mark. Name the Mistral–held proximity (55 vs 45) and why it is tolerable: the badge never sits next to a status.
   - Typeface: JetBrains Mono for the transcript and code, IBM Plex Sans for prose inside the transcript. Both are bundled through `@fontsource`, never fetched from Google Fonts. The reasons: the dashboard is served locally by `sober dashboard`, ADR 0008 keeps the browser talking only to the server, and it must work offline. The system stacks already in `--font-mono` / `--font-ui` stay as the fallbacks. The chrome outside the transcript keeps the system UI font.

2. Tokens in `apps/dashboard/src/theme.css`. Add a commented block referencing ADR 0064 in all three places: `:root` (dark), the `prefers-color-scheme: light` block and `[data-theme="light"]`. Use the mockup's values for `--tx-*`. Add `--provider-*` (the same in both themes unless contrast on light needs a darker step). Add `--font-transcript-mono: "JetBrains Mono Variable", var(--font-mono)` and `--font-transcript-sans: "IBM Plex Sans", var(--font-ui)`. OKLCH only.

3. Fonts. Add `@fontsource-variable/jetbrains-mono` and `@fontsource/ibm-plex-sans` (weights 400/500/600) to `apps/dashboard/package.json` dependencies with `pnpm --filter @besober/dashboard add`, and import them once in `apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx`. Confirm that `pnpm --filter @besober/dashboard build` still succeeds and that the font files land in the build output. Do not touch `@besober/cli`'s published dependencies. The dashboard is bundled, and ADR 0007 keeps it private.

4. Tests. Extend `test/integration/theme.test.ts`, the file that already guards ADR 0039: every `--tx-*` and `--provider-*` token must exist in the dark root and in the light block. The existing no-hex test must still pass. Add one more: no `@import` or `url(` pointing at `fonts.googleapis.com` anywhere in `apps/dashboard/src`.

acceptance.run: ls docs/adr/0064-*.md && grep -q 'ADR 0039' docs/adr/0064-*.md && grep -q -- '--tx-pass' docs/adr/0064-*.md && grep -q -- '--provider-' docs/adr/0064-*.md
acceptance.proves: the ADR exists, amends 0039, and records both exceptions including the new pass token
every transcript and provider token exists in both themes, colour stays OKLCH, and no Google Fonts URL is in the dashboard
the bundled fonts import and build cleanly

acceptance.run: ls apps/dashboard/dist/assets | grep -Eiq 'jetbrains.*\.woff2' && ls apps/dashboard/dist/assets | grep -Eiq 'plex.*\.woff2'
acceptance.proves: both typefaces are in the build output, so the dashboard works offline

acceptance.run: npx biome check apps/dashboard docs/adr test/integration/theme.test.ts
acceptance.proves: lint and format are clean for everything touched
